claims.head: Heavyweight bout
claims.body: The Blue Jackets are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Rangers are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. We think the Blue Jackets still get theirs.
claims.call: The Blue Jackets’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Rangers.
claims.nums: Columbus 5th for chance quality (a 6.6% chance of scoring on the average shot) · NY Rangers 5th for preventing dangerous shots

claims.head: The Blue Jackets will send their checkers at Zibanejad
claims.call: The Blue Jackets’ L3 (Coyle, Olivier and Sillinger) spends at least 57% of its 5-on-5 time against the Rangers’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Blue Jackets keep sending Coyle’s line (Coyle, Olivier and Sillinger) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rick Bowness has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Rangers’ first line is Zibanejad, Dorofeyev and Perreault.
claims.nums: At home: 57% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 31% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Rick Bowness likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Rangers’ first line.
claims.cite: Who plays against whom · Columbus home games this season · 4 games, 44 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

chips.tip: Columbus’s L3 (Coyle, Olivier and Sillinger) at home: 57% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ first lines. Who plays against whom, Columbus home games this season, 4 games, 44 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 31% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

check.rule: held if the share is at or above the home habit; partly if above the no-matching level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Blue Jackets can’t afford to take penalties
claims.call: The Rangers’ power play creates at least their usual 8.4 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Rangers’ power play is near the top of the league, and the Blue Jackets’ kill is one of the worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Blue Jackets more than most.
claims.nums: NY Rangers 6th for power play (8.4 expected goals per 60) · Columbus 31st for penalty kill

notes.text: Spencer Martin was added to the roster on Oct 14.
Justin Dowling was added to the roster on Oct 15 and has played beside Oliver Bjorkstrand and Jaroslav Chmelař.
Sean Durzi has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 9 games, up from 7% with his old team last season.
Ivan Provorov is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and has not played this season. He is a top-four defenseman. Zach Werenski has taken his spot beside Denton Mateychuk.

CBJ.head: Leaning the Blue Jackets’ way
CBJ.body: Columbus has been out-chancing opponents lately, has home-ice advantage and gets Andrae back. The Rangers can still swing it if their power play gets going.

NYR.head: The Rangers start a half-step behind
NYR.body: Columbus has been out-chancing opponents lately, has home-ice advantage and gets Andrae back. The Rangers’ best way to tip it is a power play that gets going.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Rangers?
paras: The Rangers come in at 6-3-0, the Blue Jackets at 2-3-0.

It’s strength against strength: the Blue Jackets are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Rangers are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. At home, Rick Bowness likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Rangers’ first line.
